newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi rejects Israel companies' advances.
newsitem.headline: Saudi rejects Israel companies' advances.

text.p: The Israel Export Institute is approaching companies in Saudi Arabia to woo investments in several of its industries, a Saudi newspaper reported on Monday.
Al-Eqtisadiah said the Saudi commerce ministry has in response instructed companies in the the world's largest oil producer and exporter to ignore the Israeli approaches.

A spokesman for the Israel Export Institute told Reuters, "Institute Director Ami Hayek expresses his dismay over the Saudi announcement and says he is certain that in the future the situation will change and there will be trade links between Israeli and Saudi companies."
The Saudi newspaper said, "Israeli one-sided contacts recently tried to woo companies, factories and Saudi businessmen."
Saudi Arabia, like most of its Gulf Arab partners, has no diplomatic or trade links with Israel. Only Oman and Qatar have established trade relations with the Jewish state.

The newspaper said the Israel Export Institute has been sending letters by mail and fax to companies mainly in Riyadh, the Red Sea port of Jeddah and the eastern province, outlining details on the plastics, irrigation and packaging industry in Israel and possibilities or joint ventures and trade exchanges.

It quoted Usamah al-Kurdi, deputy secretary-general of the Council of Saudi Chambers of Commerce, as calling on companies and businessmen to "ignore any such correspondence they receive in accordance with official instructions in this regard".

It also quoted Hamad al-Humaidan, an official at the Riyadh Chamber of Commerce and Industry, as saying that some companies in the capital had informed the chamber they were receiving such mailed letters and faxes.
